scenes.label: Meet the team
scenes.title: The Connection Lab
scenes.caption: The makers-fair guide has an editor, a reviewer and a former volunteer. Neel suggests giving everyone editing access to avoid delays. Tara points out that reading a draft, correcting it and having finished a job are three different reasons for access.
scenes.speech: The makers-fair guide has an editor, a reviewer and a former volunteer. Neel suggests giving everyone editing access to avoid delays. Tara points out that reading a draft, correcting it and having finished a job are three different reasons for access.

scenes.label: The problem
scenes.title: What changed?
scenes.caption: Least necessary access means matching permissions to the actual task. A reviewer can read without changing the master copy; an editor needs to change the working draft. A former volunteer no longer needs the shared folder merely because their name appears on an old team list.
scenes.speech: Least necessary access means matching permissions to the actual task. A reviewer can read without changing the master copy; an editor needs to change the working draft. A former volunteer no longer needs the shared folder merely because their name appears on an old team list.

scenes.label: How it works
scenes.title: Follow the evidence
scenes.caption: The teacher tests the role plan using fictional accounts and documents. Students inspect both a permitted reading action and a denied edit. They also check the end date, because a correct permission can become unnecessary when the assignment changes or the person leaves the team.
scenes.speech: The teacher tests the role plan using fictional accounts and documents. Students inspect both a permitted reading action and a denied edit. They also check the end date, because a correct permission can become unnecessary when the assignment changes or the person leaves the team.

scenes.label: Your decision
scenes.title: Decide and explain
scenes.caption: Editor changes the working draft. Reviewer reads only. Former volunteer has completed all work and has no current task. Compare the actions, then explain which evidence supports your decision.
scenes.speech: Editor changes the working draft. Reviewer reads only. Former volunteer has completed all work and has no current task. Compare the actions, then explain which evidence supports your decision.
scenes.dialogue: Which permission plan fits these jobs?

scenes.label: What changes
scenes.title: Check the consequence
scenes.caption: Give the editor editing, the reviewer reading and the former volunteer no current access. Test the plan and revisit it when the work changes or finishes.
scenes.speech: Give the editor editing, the reviewer reading and the former volunteer no current access. Test the plan and revisit it when the work changes or finishes.
scenes.dialogue: Test permitted and denied actions against a role plan.

scenes.label: Enter the lab
scenes.title: Investigate in the lab
scenes.caption: Investigate reader and editor roles, then tested permissions, then access that ends. Test your plan, read feedback and try a changed case. Save evidence; explain one limitation.
scenes.speech: Investigate reader and editor roles, then tested permissions, then access that ends. Test your plan, read feedback and try a changed case. Save evidence; explain one limitation.
scenes.dialogue: Why can a once-correct permission become unnecessary?
